profile.campus: Papillion/Springfield, Sarpy County, Nebraska (Meta's Sarpy data center campus, nine buildings planned across two municipalities)
profile.address: South 150th Street, Papillion, Sarpy County, Nebraska, 68138
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 2 of 5 mapped in this cluster) is part of Meta's Sarpy County campus straddling Papillion and Springfield, Nebraska, southwest of Omaha. Meta broke ground on the site in 2017 and has expanded it repeatedly since; as of a 2022 expansion announcement the campus plan called for nine buildings and more than 4 million square feet of data center space, up from an initial 1 million square feet, with total investment expected to exceed $1.5 billion, according to the Nebraska Examiner. An earlier 2021 expansion phase alone represented about $400 million of that investment and was expected to double Springfield's city limits. Meta has said the campus draws on 100% renewable wind energy for operations, reflecting the same net-zero, LEED Gold, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments described on Meta's own Sarpy data center fact sheet, which also reports more than $2.5 billion invested, roughly 300 operational jobs once complete, 1,300 peak skilled-trade construction workers, more than $4.1 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, and a Meta-supported project adding 320 megawatts of new renewable energy generation in Nebraska. Construction has moved more than 3 million cubic yards of dirt and used more than 6,000 tons of steel since 2017, and Meta built a highway overpass to connect sections of the growing complex. By mid-2022, more than 150 full-time employees worked across six operational buildings in Papillion, with employment expected to roughly double as three additional Springfield structures came online; construction supported about 2,000 workers at peak and continued through 2024. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual Sarpy structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

profile.regional_context: Sarpy County, in the Omaha metro area, has become a regional data center hub alongside Meta: Google operates its eighth Sarpy County facility in Papillion, and the area also hosts Fidelity, Yahoo, and other technology employers, per WOWT/Sarpy Chamber reporting. Nebraska's data center growth has been tied by local reporting to Omaha Public Power District's wind and renewable generation capacity and to state economic-development incentives for large capital investment, though this session did not confirm a specific OPPD power-purchase agreement naming Meta by facility.

reading.body:
Meta's Sarpy County campus has no published power capacity figure, so its size relative to other US data center infrastructure cannot be determined from operator specifications. The campus sits in Nebraska, a state where 21 data center facilities are mapped but none publish power specifications to this site, making Sarpy the only facility in the state with any rank at all by that metric. Meta reports $2.5 billion in cumulative investment and ground breaking in 2017, indicating long-term commitment to the site.

The facility operates buildings certified to LEED Gold standard. Meta states that electricity consumption is matched with 100 percent renewable energy as part of global net-zero operations, and that a Meta-supported project is adding 320 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity in Nebraska. These figures describe energy sourcing policy rather than the campus's own load or its contribution to state grid demand.

Without published megawatt figures, assessing whether this campus materially affects AI scaling constraints requires inference from investment scale and timeline alone. The $2.5 billion commitment and 2017 start date place it among Meta's major infrastructure plays, but the absence of any published capacity specification from Meta itself means this site cannot quantify its role in either the company's current AI training footprint or Nebraska's grid planning.
